title: Noninteractive CLI failure exit status
objective: Make uncaught compile and runtime failures from piped or redirected Sage.js CLI input exit nonzero without changing interactive REPL behavior or broken-pipe handling

oracles: Node subprocess exit-status assertions in Python and Sage modes

handoff.summary: Noninteractive REPL input now latches exit status 1 whenever an uncaught user compile, lowering, load, timing, runtime, or result-print failure is reported. TTY input retains the interactive contract of reporting errors and continuing without changing the process status. Focused CLI coverage includes successful Python input; Python and Sage runtime failures; syntax failures; an async-function failure; an EOF-flushed compound suite; a synthetic TTY session; and an early-closing stdout consumer. Independent review approved the behavior, including preservation of explicit SystemExit and EPIPE semantics.
risks: The full CLI suite now correctly fails when child Sage.js processes print uncaught tracebacks. False-green semantic tests exposed by the change are dense-prime-host-boundary, exact-polynomial-resources, exact-rational-matrix-polynomials, large-prime-polynomial, polynomial-core-correctness, polynomial-prime-evaluate, and public-sparse-random. Separately observed integration drift includes dense-matrix-public-audit, FFI generated-host/package-current checks, native-boundary ratchets, fmpz-matrix-modp-conversion, higher-weight-hecke native artifacts, and duplicate test-manifest tier membership. These failures must be corrected rather than hidden by restoring status-zero behavior.
The current portable tier is otherwise green but fails its independent manifest-integrity assertion because one host test occurs in more than one tier.
next_steps: Split the newly exposed semantic failures into focused matrix and polynomial correction lanes.
Refresh generated-artifact, native-boundary, audit-count, and test-tier expectations only after verifying their new resource surfaces are intentional.
